title: Vendor Invoice Processing for Hotels
summary: Read supplier invoices, challans and handwritten market bills, match them to purchase orders, store receipts and agreed rates, and post clean entries to accounts with exceptions flagged.

seo.title: Hotel Vendor Invoice Processing with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads hotel supplier invoices and market bills, matches them with POs, receiving records and rate lists, checks GST and posts entries to accounts.

problem.intro: A hotel buys from dozens of suppliers every week: vegetables, dairy, meat, groceries, LPG, linen laundry, housekeeping supplies and maintenance contracts. Bills arrive as GST invoices, delivery challans and handwritten market slips, and accounts match them by hand to purchase orders and the store receiving register before paying.

pain_points.title: Rates that creep
pain_points.detail: Vegetable and dairy rates are agreed weekly, but invoices arrive at different rates and nobody compares every line.

pain_points.title: Billed versus received
pain_points.detail: Short deliveries, rejected items and weight differences recorded at the receiving bay are not always deducted from the invoice.

pain_points.title: Handwritten and mixed formats
pain_points.detail: Local suppliers send handwritten bills and challans that are typed into Tally line by line.

pain_points.title: Duplicates and GST errors
pain_points.detail: The same bill is submitted twice, or tax is charged as IGST instead of CGST and SGST, which affects input tax credit.

solution.overview: We build an invoice pipeline for hotel purchasing. Invoices, challans and market slips arrive by email, as WhatsApp photos or as scans from the store. OCR and a large language model extract supplier, GSTIN, invoice number, line items, quantities, units, rates and tax. Each line is matched to the purchase order or indent, the store receiving entry and the agreed rate list for that week. The pipeline checks arithmetic, tax type and GSTIN format, and looks for duplicates. Matched invoices are prepared for posting to your accounting system, and mismatches go to an exception queue with the reason and the source document side by side.
capabilities: Extraction from GST invoices, delivery challans and handwritten market bills
Three-way match of invoice lines with purchase orders or indents and store receiving records
Rate check against weekly vegetable, dairy and meat rate lists or annual supply contracts
Short-delivery and rejected-item deductions taken from the receiving register
GSTIN format, tax type and arithmetic checks, with duplicate detection
Exception queue and posting file for Tally, Zoho Books or your ERP

workflow.title: Receive bills
workflow.detail: Invoices and challans arrive by email, as WhatsApp photos from the store or as scans, and are grouped by supplier and date.

workflow.title: Extract lines
workflow.detail: Supplier details, line items, quantities, units, rates and tax are extracted with confidence scores.

workflow.title: Match with PO and receipt
workflow.detail: Each line is matched to the purchase order or indent, the store receiving entry and the agreed rate.

workflow.title: Run checks
workflow.detail: Arithmetic, GST, duplicates, rate differences and short deliveries are checked against your tolerances.

workflow.title: Review exceptions
workflow.detail: Accounts or the purchase manager review flagged lines and record decisions or debit notes.

workflow.title: Post to accounts
workflow.detail: Approved invoices are exported to the accounting system with links to the source documents.

inputs: Supplier GST invoices and delivery challans
Store receiving register or goods receipt notes
Weekly rate lists and annual supply contracts
outputs: Structured invoice records with line items
Match status per line, with reasons for exceptions
Suggested debit notes for short deliveries and rate differences
Posting file or entries for the accounting system

human_in_the_loop: Accounts approve every exception, and the purchase manager decides on rate disputes and debit notes. Payment approval stays with the financial controller or owner, as it does today.
integrations: Tally, Zoho Books, SAP Business One or your ERP
Hotel inventory or store management module

guardrails: No invoice posted or paid without the configured approval
Every extracted value linked to the bill image
Tolerances for rates and quantities set by finance, not by the model
Duplicate checks across supplier, invoice number, date and amount
Low-confidence handwritten bills always sent for review
compliance_notes: GST checks help protect input tax credit by catching wrong tax types and invalid GSTINs before posting.
Keeps an audit trail linking each payment to its invoice, receipt and approval.

Handwritten bills processed without manual re-typing, counted against all handwritten bills received.

faqs.q: Can it read handwritten bills from local vendors?
faqs.a: Yes, for reasonably clear handwriting on typical market slips. Lines it reads with low confidence are flagged for review, and the pilot reports accuracy separately for handwritten bills.

Yes. We usually produce an import file or use Tally's integration options to create purchase entries, with a link to the bill image stored for reference. Systems such as Zoho Books or SAP Business One connect through their APIs.

faqs.q: What if we do not raise purchase orders for daily vegetables?
faqs.a: Many hotels buy daily produce against a kitchen indent and a weekly rate list. The pipeline can match against the indent, the receiving entry and the rate list instead of a PO.

faqs.q: Can it help with food cost control?
faqs.a: It produces clean, item-level purchase data by supplier and category, which feeds food cost reports. It does not replace stock counts or recipe costing, but it makes the purchase side reliable.
